topic.focus: options market signals predicting equity returns
topic.angle: put-call ratio, implied volatility skew, unusual options activity as equity filter

papers.title: Do Option Characteristics Predict the Underlying Stock Returns in the Cross-Section?
papers.hypothesis: Rank stocks by call-minus-put implied volatility spread (ATM 30-day call IV minus ATM 30-day put IV), going long high-spread stocks; this signal is the strongest single-month predictor among 30+ option characteristics.
papers.rationale: Neuhierl et al. run a comprehensive horse-race of option-implied predictors and find IV spread dominates at 1-month horizon. Construction is straightforward: average (call_IV_atm - put_IV_atm) over the last 5 trading days using 30-day maturity options. The signal captures both informed demand and short-sale pressure, making it robust to many confounds.

papers.title: Why Does Options Market Information Predict Stock Returns?
papers.source: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X25001618 (Journal of Financial Economics 2025, Muravyev, Pearson, Pollet)
papers.hypothesis: IV spread and IV skew signals lose two-thirds of their alpha once high-stock-borrow-fee stocks are excluded, suggesting the options signal mostly proxies for short-sale constraints rather than private information.
papers.rationale: This is an important negative result for implementation: the raw IV spread signal survives only in hard-to-borrow stocks that are costly or impossible to short in practice. For a long-only cross-sectional momentum strategy, this suggests filtering on the long side using IV spread (avoid high IV-spread stocks rather than shorting them) is the actionable modification. The signal retains modest predictive power even in liquid, easy-to-borrow names.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Variation of Option-Implied Volatility Skew
papers.hypothesis: Decompose IV skew into a structural (slow-moving, risk-based) component and a transient (fast-moving, information-based) component; rank stocks on the transient skew residual, going long stocks with the lowest transient skew (least negative sentiment).
techniques: OTM put minus ATM call IV
papers.rationale: Standard IV skew (delta=-0.25 OTM put IV minus delta=-0.50 ATM call IV, 30-day expiry) mixes two signals: structural firm risk and transient informed flow. Wu & Tian show the transient residual — computed by cross-sectionally regressing current skew on lagged structural proxies — carries the incremental predictive content. Using a 63-day lookback to estimate the structural baseline and a 5-day skip avoids short-term reversal. This is directly implementable as a secondary ranking layer on top of price momentum.

papers.title: Unusual Option Activity: Is it Smart to Follow 'Smart Money'?
papers.hypothesis: Identify stocks with unusually large increases in OTM put open interest relative to their 63-day baseline and use this as a negative filter (downweight or exclude these stocks from the long book).
papers.rationale: Jiang and Strong define unusual activity as OI changes exceeding 2 standard deviations of recent history, weighted by option moneyness (OTM puts carry the strongest signal). Stocks with unusual put OI spikes underperform the next month by ~60 bps risk-adjusted. As a negative filter on a momentum long book it is low-cost to implement: compute (put_OI_today - MA63_put_OI) / std63_put_OI per stock and exclude the top 5% spike decile from longs.

papers.title: Stock Return Predictability of the Realized-Implied Volatility Spread
papers.hypothesis: Rank stocks by RVol-IVol spread (22-day realized vol minus 30-day ATM implied vol); stocks where realized vol exceeds implied vol (positive spread) predict higher future returns, consistent with priced volatility risk.
papers.rationale: The RVol-IVol spread proxies the individual stock variance risk premium: a positive spread means the market is overpricing vol protection relative to realized, implying the stock has been less risky than feared. Sorted portfolios long top-decile (positive spread) minus bottom-decile earn ~5% annualized alpha in US equities 2000-2023. The signal is computed purely from OHLC prices and a single ATM IV observation per stock, making it feasible even with partial options coverage in the Russell 1000 universe.
